name: answer_charge
description: Write or update a charge answer file in research/charges/. Synthesises from existing concepts and reports only — does not fetch external sources. Updates CHARGE.md with the link. Mutating — requires human confirmation before writing.

charge_question.description: The exact charge question text from CHARGE.md (for the charge file header).

status.description: Answered = clear defensible answer exists. Partial = main thrust answered, sub-questions remain. Open = insufficient research to answer.

answer.description: Direct answer to the charge question. Commit to a position — not 'it depends' without follow-up. For Open status, state what is known and what is needed.

citation.description: Inline citation in format '[→ report-slug.md §Section Title]' or '[→ concepts/concept-slug.md §Section]'.

claim.description: The specific claim or finding from that source that supports the answer.

evidence.description: Evidence items supporting the answer, each citing a specific section of an existing concepts/ or reports/ file.

open_questions.description: Residual open questions — what is still unknown or unresolved after synthesising the research.

primary_sources.description: Kebab slugs of the concept/report files that are primary sources for this charge answer.

examples.description: Answer a charge question about skill security with partial confidence

input.charge_question: What trust and security model should AKH use for community-submitted skills?
input.answer: AKH should adopt Hermes's four-tier trust model (builtin / trusted / community / agent-created) with a mandatory regex security scan at install time using the six threat categories defined in skills_guard.py. The 'trusted' tier should be reserved for Anthropic and a small set of vetted publishers. Community skills with any scan finding should be blocked by default, with an explicit --force override available to users.

evidence.claim: skills_guard.py implements 6 threat categories (exfiltration, injection, destructive, persistence, network, obfuscation) with trust-aware install policy — community skills blocked on any finding
SkillNet has no security scan at install time — AKH should not follow this pattern

open_questions: What publishers should be in the 'trusted' tier for SLAC's AKH instance?
Does the scan need to cover compiled binaries or only Markdown/Python?
